summary: Honor explicitly assigned, policy-approved organization-read access in neutral Cloud account sessions without granting platform write authority.
userImpact: Ordinary signup accounts retain only their existing self-onboarding authority; no organization-read grant is created automatically.

instructions: Deploy the qualified host revision alongside the compatible Cloud composition; existing role assignments and policy gates remain authoritative.

configuration: An authorized application administrator must explicitly assign platform:tenants:view; GCP roles and an email address alone do not confer this permission.

changes: Cloud-account permission snapshots may advertise platform.tenants.read only when the current global permission and policy allow it.
The existing platform Cloud identity exchange can mint a one-use read claim for that account; manage claims remain forbidden.

notes: No role, assignment, account, or schema is created or changed by this code upgrade.

security: Permission and policy are rechecked on every snapshot and identity request, with no tenant-scoped authority promoted to platform access.
Neutral sessions still cannot mint platform management claims or acquire tenant, project, engine, or unrelated administration rights.
documentation: docs/how-to/auth-sso.md documents the account-session authorization boundary.
knownLimitations: This does not apply an operator grant or recover a blocked Cloud deployment; those are separate authorized actions.
Already-issued platform read claims retain the existing one-use, 90-second lifetime; revocation stops new claims rather than changing that contract.
rollback: Roll back the host revision to restore the previous account-surface restriction; existing durable grants are unchanged.
validation: Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 11.0.8: 108 focused authorization-route tests cover explicit grant, default denial, policy denial and revocation. The complete backend milestone passed all 3,799 tests across 467 files, and the raw-SQL guard passed; original assertions and timeouts were preserved.

Host build, workspace typechecking, access-governance structure, identity contracts/routes/components and provisioning checks passed. Physical PostgreSQL acceptance includes 22 global OIDC/RLS tests, the managed-account session test and the independent authorization model's 24 generated states, with forced RLS and original bounds retained. This is not five-adapter portability acceptance.

All 18 Chromium lifecycle/login-gallery cases passed on an isolated loopback fixture. Screenshot capture now preserves visible mapping results; all 29 selected 1440x900 images passed duplicate/dimension audit and visual review. These mocked browser flows are not live Cloud signup evidence.

The full disposable compiled-stack protocol rehearsal passed ten SCIM, OIDC, Entra-compatible OIDC, signed SAML and LDAP/TLS journeys. Production-client LDAPS tests also passed. Owned fixtures and temporary credentials were removed; local provider/directory evidence is not a real external-provider or Cloud signup receipt.

All five plugin/API and three host packages built and packed locally; tarball exports/dependency references, backend-host 0.20.1 version discipline, documentation boundary and release-note preflight passed against v0.30.0. Local packaging checks are not signed release provenance.

Protected exact-candidate database, pinned Operaton/browser, image and current security acceptance remain independent of local qualification. No release publication, staging deployment or live Cloud E2E acceptance is claimed.
